[Follow us](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=kiplinger.com). A handful of central bank officials will speak this week, with the quiet period around [Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting as Fed chair](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/economy/3-ways-kevin-warsh-will-change-the-fed) set to begin at 12 am Eastern Standard Time on Saturday, June 6. [Sign up](https://www.kiplinger.com/newsletter). Markets will monitor this week's Fed speeches and incoming employment market data for information about what a Warsh Fed will do with the [federal funds rate](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/what-is-the-federal-funds-rate) amid persistent [inflation](https://www.kiplinger.com/economic-forecasts/inflation). **Friday, June 5: Nonfarm payrolls report:** We saw sharp gains in the [April jobs report](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/economy/jobs-report-april-2026-what-to-expect) following a strong March. * [Kiplinger's Earnings Calendar](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/stocks/17494/next-week-earnings-calendar-stocks). * [Kiplinger's Economic Forecasts](https://www.kiplinger.com/economic-forecasts). * [Stock Market Holidays in 2026](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/stock-market-holidays). * [Stock Market Trading Hours](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/602886/stock-market-trading-hours). [Home](https://schwabnetwork.com)[Articles](https://schwabnetwork.com/articles)Top Economic Data to Watch Week of June 1, 2026. However, this week the focus shifts to economic data, earnings from several cybersecurity and semiconductor companies, and the [potential deal between the U.S. and Iran](https://schwabnetwork.com/video/geopolitics-and-oil-aarathi-krishnan-on-the-u-s-iran-disconnect). As May data trickle in, markets will focus on the direction of [inflation, the labor market, and key sentiment](https://schwabnetwork.com/video/looking-past-the-headlines-lance-mcgray-on-inflation-and-rates) indicators across major U.S. industries. On the economic data front, Monday kicks off the week with a look into the industrial economy via the ISM Manufacturing PMI. Two components within this report will be of key focus: the headline PMI number, which over the last several months has reflected improvement in the manufacturing industry among the purchasing managers surveyed, and the ISM Manufacturing Prices component. Consensus expectations call for ADP to come in at 110,000 jobs added for the month of May. The week closes with the BLS Employment Report, where the market is expecting Nonfarm Employment Change of 95,000 jobs added for the month and an unemployment rate of 4.3%.
